texts.facts: In backdrop, Sh.B.P.Saroha, Food Safety Officer purchased a sample of Noodles, an article of food for analysis from Sh.Sandeep Kumar s/o Sh. G.N.Singh of M/s Food Bazar, Unit of Future Retail Ltd., Rajendra Place, Metro Station, New Delhi 110008 on 05.06.2015 where the said food article was found stored for sale and for human consumption. The sample was taken as per order and direction of Designated Officer. Each counterpart of the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to FSS Act. Notice in Form VA was given to Sh.Sandeep Kumar and price of sample was duly paid. One part of the sample was sent to Food Analyst for analysis on 08.06.2015. The FBO did not request to send the fourth part of the sample for analysis from an NABL Accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 ("FSS Rules" in short). Thus, the remaining two counter parts and the fourth counter part were deposited with the Designated Officer. The Food Analyst vide his report no.FSS/265/2015 dated 22.06.2015 reported that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.3 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 ( "FSS (P&L) Regulations" in short). The Food Analyst has also reported regarding the label "No Added MSG" which is misleading. The Designated Officer sent a copy of Food Analyst report to FBO Sh.Sandeep Kumar and also to manufacturer M/s Capital Food Pvt. Ltd. for giving them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of Food Analyst. However, the FBO and manufacturer did not prefer any appeal. During the proceedings, M/s Food Bazar (Unit of Future Retail Ltd.) appointed Sh.Kuldeep Singh Bisht their nominee, supplier company M/s Rajkala Industries Pvt. Ltd. appointed Sh. Adityavikram Adukia their nominee and manufacturer M/s Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd. appointed Sh. Manish Shrivastava their nominee. The FSO filed an application under Rule 3.1.1(3) of FSS Rules for violation of Section 52 of FSS Act.
texts.arguments: The appellants have challenged the impugned order on the ground that the Ld.A.O. has passed the impugned order mechanically without taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case. It has been submitted that as per the opinion of Food Analyst, the sample is misbranded M/S Capital Foods Pvt. Ltd vs State on 19 October, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167944077/ 2 because there is violation of Regulation 2.2.1.3 of FSS(P&L) Regulations. It has been submitted that as per the report of Food Analyst, the monosodium glutamate (MSG) was found nil in the sample food commodity and therefore, in view of this report, the declaration of "No Added MSG" on the label cannot constitute misbranding. Ld.Counsel has relied upon the documents of the FSSAI i.e. FSSAI File No: 1 (105) Maggi Noodles/2015/FSSAI(PartI) wherein it has been interalia held that: "To prevent, both avoidable harassment/prosecution of Food Business Operators (FBOs) as well as to ensure that the consumers are facilitated to exercise informed choices in respect of what they eat, proceedings may be launched against FBOs only when the labels states "No MSG" or "No added MSG" and MSG is actually found in the impugned foodstuff." Ld.Counsel has also relied upon I.T.C. Limited vs State of M.P. and Ors., (W.P. No.5427 of 2016) wherein it was interalia held as under: "15/In the present case record reveals that there was no basis to prosecute the petitioner for the alleged offence as no MSG was found in the sample, therefore, there was no misbranding by the petitioner. The petitioner could have been said to have committed offence if after mentioning 'No Added MSG' in the sample it was found that MSG was added but that is not so. This issue was specifically raised by the petitioner before the adjudicating authority but the same has not been properly considered while passing the impugned order dated 26.07.2016 , therefor, the impugned order cannot be sustained.
